solution: The integrating factor is $e^{\int 2dx}=e^{2x}$. Then $\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{2x}y)=e^{2x}e^{-x}=e^{x}$. Integrating, $e^{2x}y=e^{x}+C$, so $y=e^{-x}+Ce^{-2x}$. Check: $y'+2y=(-e^{-x}-2Ce^{-2x})+2(e^{-x}+Ce^{-2x})=e^{-x}$.
